title: Where Is It, in Which Frame: A Tree of Coordinate Frames and the Transform at the Right Time

questions.question: A laser sees an obstacle 1 m ahead of itself. What must be known to put it on the map?
options: The chain of frames from the laser up to the map, each a transform: the laser on the base, the base in odom, odom in the map
questions.explanation: The obstacle was at (12.00, 6.30) in the map in the test.

questions.question: Halfway between headings of 170 and -170 degrees. What is it?
options: 180: the short way round, where averaging as plain numbers would give 0 and point the opposite way
questions.explanation: The blend takes the difference, wraps it, then goes part of the way.

questions.question: How does a lookup relate two frames on different branches?
options: Via the nearest frame they both hang from, compose(inverse(target_from_common), source_from_common)
questions.explanation: The arm in the laser's frame was found at (-0.4, 0.2).

questions.question: A robot drives at 0.6 m/s and a scan stamped 0.5 s ago is placed with the latest transform. How far out is every obstacle?
options: 0.30 m, speed times delay, in the direction of travel
questions.explanation: The transform at the stamp placed the post at 2.60 and the latest at 2.90.

questions.question: A frame was reported until 1.0 s and a lookup asks about 1.5 s. What should happen?
options: Extend it at its last speed
extrapolation: a refusal, since nobody measured the robot then and a guess would look like data
questions.explanation: The lookup says which of three things is wrong.

questions.question: What does a static frame mean?
options: It is not in the tree
It does not move relative to its parent, such as a sensor mount, and is known at every time
questions.explanation: The laser and the arm were static.
